name: ⭐ Rust
desc: A fast, memory-safe systems language that uses ownership and compile-time borrow checking instead of a garbage collector, preventing data races and many memory bugs while keeping C/C++-level performance.

name: ⭐ Go
desc: A simple, compiled language designed for reliable and efficient software, with lightweight goroutines and channels making concurrency easy, plus fast builds and single-binary deployment.

name: Zig
desc: An explicit systems language positioned as a modern C replacement, offering manual memory management, compile-time execution via comptime, no hidden control flow, and seamless C interoperability.

name: JavaScript
desc: A dynamic, event-driven language with JIT execution, essential for the web browser and widely used on servers via Node.js, ideal for interactive UIs and async I/O.

name: TypeScript
desc: A statically typed superset of JavaScript that compiles to plain JS, adding type checking and better tooling for large-scale applications while retaining JavaScript’s ecosystem and runtime behavior.

name: C
desc: A minimal, close-to-hardware procedural language with a simple mapping to machine code, still foundational for operating systems, embedded systems, and performance-critical libraries.

name: C++
desc: An extension of C adding object-oriented, generic, and functional programming with zero-overhead abstractions, widely used for game engines, trading systems, and large high-performance software.

name: PHP
desc: A dynamic, server-side scripting language built for the web, embedded directly in HTML and powering most CMS platforms; modern PHP 8 adds strong performance, a JIT, and type improvements while remaining easy to deploy on standard hosting.

name: Kotlin
desc: A concise, statically typed language by JetBrains that runs on the JVM and interoperates fully with Java, offering null safety, coroutines, and multiplatform support; it’s the preferred language for Android and increasingly used for backend and cross-platform development.

name: Swift
desc: A fast, safe, and expressive compiled language by Apple with optionals, automatic reference counting, and protocol-oriented design; it’s the primary language for iOS, macOS, watchOS, and tvOS development via SwiftUI/UIKit, and also usable for server-side and cross-platform work.
